stories.headline: OpenAI says unreleased Astra solved 10 open math problems; Anthropic researcher redoes 5 with Fable

key_facts.fact: OpenAI revealed on Saturday, August 1, that an internal version of Astra, the model family it calls its next major release, produced new results on 10 problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science that had been open for at least a decade, published with machine-checkable proofs.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI Group PBC revealed Saturday that an internal version of Astra, the model family it calls its next major release, produced new results for 10 problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science that had been open for at least a decade, and it published machine-checkable proofs alongside the claim.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI research scientist Noam Brown posted that the internal Astra version 'solved 10 major open problems in mathematics, quantum complexity, and theoretical computer science' and called it 'a major step for scientific reasoning'.
key_facts.excerpt: An internal version of Astra, @OpenAI's next major model family, solved 10 major open problems in mathematics, quantum complexity, and theoretical computer science. We believe it will be a major step for scientific reasoning.

key_facts.fact: The proofs ship with Lean 4 certificates; Thomas Bloom, the mathematician who in October 2025 called OpenAI's earlier Erdős-problem claim 'a dramatic misrepresentation', called this result 'big news'.
key_facts.excerpt: the proofs are formalized in Lean 4 with machine-checkable certificates that any reader can verify; and Bloom himself — the researcher who dismantled the 2025 claim — called this result 'big news'

key_facts.fact: Astra is described by OpenAI as a multi-agent system in which a root agent creates subagents and synthesizes their results, built for long-horizon tasks running hours or days; Sam Altman demonstrated it in closed-door Washington meetings on July 29, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: It is a multi-agent system: a root agent creates subagents, distributes portions of a problem, waits for results, and synthesizes a final answer — a design built for long-horizon tasks that can run for hours or days on a single objective... Sam Altman demonstrated Astra in closed-door meetings with senators and senior administration officials in Washington on July 29, 2026

key_facts.fact: Anthropic engineer Levent Alpoge said on X that within 24 hours he reproduced five of the same results using the publicly available Claude Fable, autonomously and with generic prompts and no internet access, including arithmetic circuit complexity, quantum parallel repetition and the closest vector problem.
key_facts.excerpt: Shortly after OpenAI's blog post, Anthropic engineer Levent Alpoge responded. In an X post, Levent claimed that he was able to solve 5 of the same problems with Claude Fable, a model already available to the public, in under 24 hours... Some of the problems he claims to have solved with Fable include arithmetic circuit complexity, quantum parallel repetition, and closest vector problem.

key_facts.fact: Gary Marcus argued the announcement was 'marketing, not science', noting OpenAI did not say how many conjectures were attempted and that the advertised $2,000 total compute cost likely counts only the successful runs.
key_facts.excerpt: Yesterday's tweet and blog were marketing, not science... First: How many conjectures were attempted?... loudly that this was done for a total computation cost of $2000. It seems a safe bet that this includes only the conjectures where Astra succeeded, not the ones where it failed.

key_facts.fact: Astra remains unreleased, with no release date, pricing, or decision on whether it ships as GPT-6 or another GPT-5 variant, and any launch runs through the US federal AI safety review process.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has not given a release date, pricing or a decision on whether the model ships as GPT-6 or as another GPT-5 variant, and any launch will run through the federal AI safety review process that already staggered the GPT-5.6 rollout.

stories.headline: Alibaba launches Qwen3.8-Max, a 2.4T-parameter flagship, and will open its weights next week

key_facts.fact: Alibaba announced Qwen3.8-Max on Monday, August 3: 2.4 trillion total parameters with only 95 billion activated, a sparse mixture-of-experts design with hybrid attention and a 1 million token context window.
key_facts.excerpt: Boasting 2.4 trillion parameters and supporting a context window of up to 1 million tokens... Despite its total size of 2.4 trillion parameters, Qwen3.8-Max activates just 95 billion parameters.

key_facts.fact: It is the first Qwen-Max-class model whose weights will be released publicly; the weights for Qwen3.8-Max and a smaller Qwen3.8-27B are due on Hugging Face and ModelScope next week.
key_facts.excerpt: This also marks the first time we will open-source the weights of a Qwen-Max-class model — the open weights will be released next week... The model weights will be open-sourced on Hugging Face and ModelScope next week.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba says the model ranks fifth in Text Arena and second in Vision Arena and is available via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio APIs and its QwenWork agent platform.
key_facts.excerpt: Qwen3.8-Max ranks fifth in Text Arena and second in Vision Arena... The model is now accessible via APIs on the Alibaba Cloud Model Studio for global developers, with model weights scheduled for release next week.

key_facts.fact: Self-reported benchmarks put it at 86.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (ahead of Claude Opus 4.8 and Claude Fable 5 at 84.6, behind GPT-5.6 Sol at 88.8), 93.0 on PaperBench and 92.6 on GPQA Diamond, with pricing of $2 per 1M input tokens and $6 per 1M output.
key_facts.excerpt: Qwen3.8-Max scores 86.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, ahead of Claude Opus 4.8 and Claude Fable 5 at 84.6, behind GPT-5.6 Sol (max) at 88.8... It leads PaperBench at 93.0 and IFBench at 82.8. GPQA Diamond lands at 92.6... Pricing is $2 input, $6 output and $0.25 cached input per 1M tokens.

key_facts.fact: In one demonstration the model spent roughly five days on a research paper, writing 7,600 lines of code and running 33 GPU training jobs, reproducing all six of the paper's main results before testing 18 ideas of its own.
key_facts.excerpt: Over roughly five days... -Max wrote 7,600 [lines] of code and ran 33 GPU training jobs, according to the team. It first reproduced all six of the paper's main results. Then it tested 18 of its own ideas across four rounds and beat the paper

key_facts.fact: Alibaba's Hong Kong-listed shares rose 7% after the release, closing at HK$125.20, and the model is slightly smaller than Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, released in July with 2.8 trillion parameters.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's Hong Kong-listed shares rose 7 per cent following the release, closing at HK$125.20 the same day.

key_facts.fact: The model supports both OpenAI's Chat Completions format and Anthropic's API protocol, so it plugs into Claude Code, Codex and other agent tooling with no code change.
key_facts.excerpt: The model supports both OpenAI's Chat Completions format and Anthropic's API protocol, so it plugs directly into Claude Code, Codex, Qoder CLI, Qwen Code, and OpenClaw.

stories.headline: EU gains power to inspect, restrict and fine AI models as AI Act enforcement kicks in

key_facts.fact: The European Commission's enforcement powers over general-purpose AI models took effect on Sunday, August 2, 2026, letting it demand to evaluate models before public release in the region, restrict EU market access and fine providers.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the powers that came into effect on Sunday, the Commission, the EU's executive arm, can demand to evaluate models before public release in the region, restrict EU market access and fine a provider up to 15 million euros or 3% of its annual turnover, whichever is higher.

key_facts.fact: Fines can reach €15 million or 3% of annual worldwide turnover, whichever is higher, and apply to any company offering a general-purpose AI model in the EU regardless of where it is based — putting Anthropic, OpenAI and Google in scope.
key_facts.excerpt: gaining new powers to inspect models, restrict access to the European market, and fine providers up to €15 million or 3% of annual turnover, whichever is higher... cover every company that makes a general-purpose AI model available in the E.U., no matter where that company is headquartered

key_facts.fact: Sidley Austin partner Elisabetta Righini said liability is not limited to substantive breaches: 'refusing an information request, giving misleading answers, or blocking a model evaluation is fineable on its own', and non-EU providers must appoint an EU-based authorised representative.
key_facts.excerpt: "What's rarely appreciated is that GPAI liability isn't limited to substantive breaches: refusing an information request, giving misleading answers, or blocking a model evaluation is fineable on its own," she said. Righini also noted that companies headquartered outside the E.U. are required to designate a local representative

key_facts.fact: The EU has opened discussions with OpenAI and Anthropic in the wake of cyberattacks linked to their models; Anthropic agreed to give the EU cybersecurity agency ENISA access to its Mythos model after Commission officials pressed its leadership in San Francisco.
key_facts.excerpt: The E.U. has also opened discussions with OpenAI and Anthropic in the wake of cyber attacks that have been linked to their models, according to CNBC... Anthropic agreed to give the EU's cybersecurity agency ENISA access to its Mythos model after senior Commission officials traveled to San Francisco to press Anthropic leadership directly

key_facts.fact: The obligations themselves (documentation, copyright policy, training-data summaries, systemic-risk mitigation) have applied since August 2, 2025, but the Commission had no power to act on them during that first year; the AI Office now holds exclusive supervisory authority over GPAI models.
key_facts.excerpt: The enforcement powers of the AI Office and the national competent authorities of the Member States apply from 2 August 2026, when certain provisions of the AI Act become enforceable.

key_facts.fact: The new powers land amid EU-US friction: after the bloc fined Google $1 billion in July under Digital Markets Act rules, President Donald Trump threatened the EU with a 'substantial' tariff.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened the EU with a "substantial" tariff after the bloc hit Google with a $1 billion fine in July, under Digital Markets Act rules.

stories.headline: Artificial Analysis: DeepSeek V4-Flash is the cheapest known model to run, 100x below Fable 5

key_facts.excerpt: A version of DeepSeek's flagship AI model is now the least expensive well-known system to run on benchmark tests anywhere in the world. According to research firm Artificial Analysis, it costs more than 100 times less to operate than Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.

key_facts.fact: V4-Flash charges $0.14 per million input tokens and $0.28 per million output tokens, working out to roughly 3 cents per benchmark test.
key_facts.excerpt: V4-Flash charges $0.14 per million input tokens and $0.28 per million output tokens, working out to roughly 3 cents per test.

key_facts.fact: On the same cost-per-test measure, Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 runs at 86 cents, OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol at $1.86 and Claude Fable 5 at $3.15.
key_facts.excerpt: Artificial Analysis estimated the average cost of running V4-Flash at three cents per test, compared with $0.86 for Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, $1.86 for OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and $3.15 for Claude Fable 5.

key_facts.fact: Artificial Analysis says it cost $57.85 in total to evaluate DeepSeek V4 Flash on its Intelligence Index, and the model's blended rate works out to $0.08 per 1M tokens on a 7:2:1 cache/input/output mix.
key_facts.excerpt: In total, it cost $57.85 to evaluate DeepSeek V4 Flash (Reasoning, High Effort) on the Intelligence Index... For a blended rate (7:2:1 cache hit/input/output ratio), this is $0.08 per 1M tokens.

stories.headline: Report says Nvidia cut Rubin Ultra's memory to 192GB; Samsung and SK hynix drop 8%

key_facts.fact: SemiAnalysis research dated July 29 says the mainstream Rubin Ultra SKU now uses HBM4 8-Hi at 192GB and about 21TB/s, down from the 288GB 12-Hi HBM4 of the standard Rubin, with the same 35 PFLOPs peak compute
key_facts.excerpt: SemiAnalysis research dated July 29 says the mainstream Ultra SKU uses HBM4 8-Hi, 192GB, approximately 21TB/s, and 1,800W Max-Q, with the same peak theoretical FLOPs as Rubin and the principal upgrade shifting to a 576-GPU scale-up domain

key_facts.fact: The only major upgrade is interconnect scale: Rubin Ultra supports NVL576, linking up to 576 GPUs over NVLink versus 72 for the standard Rubin
key_facts.excerpt: The spec highlight shifts to 'expanded interconnect scale': supporting the NVL576 architecture, up to 576 GPUs can be interconnected to form a super logical GPU—8x the scale of the standard 72-card configuration.

key_facts.fact: SemiAnalysis calculates HBM's share of a Rubin Ultra rack's bill of materials falls from nearly 40% to 28% while interconnect rises from 4% to 12%, cutting per-rack BOM from roughly $8 million back to about $6.4 million
key_facts.excerpt: Cost optimization at the core: HBM's share of total cost drops from nearly 40% to 28%, while interconnect cost share rises from 4% to 12%; per-rack bill of materials falls from roughly $8 million to $6.4 million.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia has not publicly confirmed the Rubin Ultra specifications reported by SemiAnalysis; it has confirmed only the current Rubin's 288GB HBM4 and the Ultra NVL576 8x72-GPU topology
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia has currently confirmed only the existing Rubin specifications of 288GB HBM4, 12-Hi, and 22TB/s, as well as Ultra NVL576's 8×72-GPU topology, and has not yet confirmed the aforementioned Ultra specifications.

key_facts.excerpt: The company completed an approximately $80.5 million Series C round in May 2024, which set its post-money valuation at $529 million ... The company has now raised approximately $103 million to $104 million in total funding across all rounds.

key_facts.fact: DeepX signed more than 30 purchase orders within seven months of mass-producing its first-generation DX-M1 chip, targets about $40 million of revenue this year and plans an IPO once the Series D closes
key_facts.excerpt: DeepX ... has signed more than 30 purchase order contracts within seven months of mass-producing its first-generation chip ... The company is targeting revenue of approximately $40 million (about 59.2 billion won) this year. Once its ongoing Series D funding round is completed, the company plans to pursue an initial public offering.

stories.headline: Four US states scrap data center tax breaks and nine more weigh repeal, lifting equipment costs 7%

key_facts.fact: The Information reported on August 2 that data center equipment costs could rise more than 7% as the repeal of state tax breaks spreads
key_facts.excerpt: The Information reported on the 2nd that equipment costs could increase by more than 7% as the move to repeal data center tax breaks spreads among state governments.

key_facts.fact: In a state with a 7% sales tax, ending the exemption would push the IT equipment bill for a gigawatt-class data center from $40 billion to $43 billion
key_facts.excerpt: In states with a 7% sales tax, the elimination of tax breaks is expected to push the cost of building the information technology (IT) equipment for a gigawatt (GW)-class data center from 40 billion dollars to 43 billion dollars.

key_facts.fact: Four states have enacted rollbacks or suspensions and at least nine more are weighing similar action, per an analysis published Monday
key_facts.excerpt: A comprehensive analysis published Monday compiled the scope of the national rollback: four US states have now repealed or suspended data center sales tax exemptions, and at least nine more are actively weighing similar action.

key_facts.fact: Arizona enacted a three-year moratorium on new exemption applications through June 2029; Illinois paused new incentive agreements from July 1; North Carolina repealed its electricity tax exemption for data centers outright
key_facts.excerpt: Arizona enacted a three-year moratorium on new exemption applications, running from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2029 ... Illinois Governor JB Pritzker directed the state Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity to pause processing new data center incentive agreements starting July 1 ... North Carolina repealed its electricity tax exemption for data centers outright through its 2026 budget.

key_facts.fact: Georgia's exemption cost $2.5 billion in fiscal 2026, 664% above the state's estimate, and a University of Georgia audit found roughly 70% of the projects would have located there anyway; Ohio lost $1.6 billion in fiscal 2025, nearly 12 times its projection
key_facts.excerpt: The final tally for fiscal year 2026 came in at $2.5 billion — 664 percent above Georgia's estimate ... roughly 70 percent of the data center projects receiving the exemption would have located in Georgia even without it ... the state lost $555 million in fiscal year 2024 and $1.6 billion in fiscal year 2025 — nearly 12 times the projected cost.

key_facts.fact: Rack power density explains the blowout: pre-AI racks drew 5 to 15 kilowatts, while AI-optimized racks draw 120 kilowatts or more, multiplying the value of every tax-free equipment purchase
key_facts.excerpt: Data center rack power density has risen from 5 to 15 kilowatts in the pre-AI era to 120 kilowatts or more for AI-optimized racks — an 8 to 24-times increase that multiplied the investment value of every qualifying purchase

key_facts.fact: The National Conference of State Legislatures counts 13 to 14 states — including Arizona, Connecticut, Georgia, Maryland, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Virginia and Texas — that have abolished or suspended data center sales taxes or plan to
key_facts.excerpt: According to the National Conference of State Legislatures (NCSL) ... 13 to 14 states, including Arizona, Connecticut, Georgia, Maryland, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Virginia and Texas, have already abolished or suspended their data center sales taxes or plan to do so.

stories.headline: Korea's Robotis open-sources the full control software of its AI Sapiens humanoid

key_facts.fact: Robotis said on August 3 it is the first company in Korea to fully release the entire software of its humanoid robot 'AI Sapiens'
key_facts.excerpt: Robotis (108490.KQ) has become the first company in Korea to fully release the entire software of its humanoid robot "AI Sapiens," seeking to build an ecosystem that allows anyone to develop humanoids quickly and easily.

key_facts.fact: The release includes Sim2Real tools and reinforcement learning workflows that automate transferring walking ability trained in Nvidia's simulation environment to the physical robot
key_facts.excerpt: the released materials include "Sim2Real" (simulation-to-reality transfer) tools and reinforcement learning workflows, considered the greatest challenge in humanoid development ... transferring a robot's walking ability—refined through repeated training in NVIDIA's simulation environment—to real-world settings without error.

key_facts.fact: The humanoid industry has typically exposed only limited APIs while keeping balance and locomotion control code secret; Robotis released the full driving code under a license with minimal commercial restrictions, requiring no separate contract
key_facts.excerpt: Until now, the humanoid industry has provided only simple application programming interfaces (APIs) ... while keeping strictly secret the core control code governing how a robot actually maintains balance and walks ... By adopting a license with the fewest restrictions on commercial use, users do not need to sign a separate contract with Robotis

key_facts.fact: Robotis plans to sequentially release hardware materials too, including mechanical design blueprints and electronic circuit documents, aiming for a fully open humanoid platform
key_facts.excerpt: Robotis plans to sequentially release hardware areas as well, including robot mechanical design blueprints and electronic circuit materials. Its ultimate goal is to complete a fully open platform

key_facts.fact: CEO Kim Byoung-soo framed the move as a response to Chinese humanoid makers backed by 'enormous capital and volume', saying Robotis's edge is platform openness and actuator quality
key_facts.excerpt: "The Chinese pursuit in the global robot market is fierce, but we hold a clear advantage in the fundamental openness of our platform and the overwhelming quality of our actuators," Robotis CEO Kim Byoung-soo said.

sources.title: Robotis Unveils Humanoid Software, Aiming to Expand Robot Ecosystem

stories.headline: Trump calls off 'biggest attack since WWII' on Iran; Tehran denies talks have started

key_facts.fact: In a Truth Social post on Saturday evening, Aug 1, Trump said he had cancelled a planned attack after Iran and other Middle Eastern countries asked for time, saying 'the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to'.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump in a Saturday evening social media post claimed that Mideast allies have reached the parameters of a deal to end the Iran war and said that he would hold off on ordering new strikes in the five-month old conflict for now.

key_facts.fact: Trump said the emerging deal would include the 'Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran's nuclear threat'.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal would include the immediate and complete reopening of the strait and 'an end to Iran's nuclear threat', he posted.

key_facts.fact: Speaking on Air Force One on Sunday, Aug 2, Trump said the cancelled strikes were going to be 'the biggest attack since World War II' and that negotiations with Iran would begin Monday afternoon.
key_facts.excerpt: Speaking on Air Force One on Sunday, Trump said the canceled strikes were going to be 'the biggest attack since World War II.' The president said that the U.S. is 'holding' what would have been a 'massive attack,' but that it could still take place 'anytime we want.'

key_facts.fact: Iran said on Monday, Aug 3, that it is not currently holding talks with the US, only discussions with Oman over a temporary safe route through the Strait of Hormuz; spokesman Esmail Baghaei said the route talks are a separate matter from opening or closing the strait.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran said Monday it was not currently holding talks with the U.S. but was in discussions with Oman over a temporary safe route through the strait. ... Those talks have revolved around creating a new route that would be one path with entry and exit lanes, Baghaei said Monday.

key_facts.fact: IRGC-affiliated Fars News denied on Aug 2 that Iran had accepted a Qatari-brokered plan to reopen the strait, quoting a source saying it stays closed as long as the US continues 'hostile actions', while Fars aired footage of vessels 'waiting for permission' to transit.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's semiofficial Fars news agency aired footage Sunday of what it said were vessels 'waiting for permission' from Iran to transit through the Strait of Hormuz. ... The waterway will remain closed as long as 'the United States continues its hostile actions,' the source stressed.

key_facts.fact: ISW reported on Aug 2 that Qatari mediators presented Iran a new proposal under which vessels would enter the Gulf through Iranian waters and exit through Omani waters, and that Iranian diplomats responded positively, while IRGC hardliners appear to reject any arrangement reducing Iranian control of the waterway.
key_facts.excerpt: Israeli media also reported on August 2 that Araghchi agreed to a US- and Qatari-formulated proposal in which vessels would enter the Persian Gulf through Iranian waters and exit through Omani waters.

key_facts.fact: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman phoned Trump on Saturday to press for de-escalation, warning of the risk that Iran would retaliate against Gulf energy infrastructure; the war, which began Feb 28, is now in its sixth month.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince, Mohammed bin Salman, spoke on the phone with Trump before his announcement ... he stressed the need ... prioritise dialogue 'to reduce escalation'.

stories.headline: OPEC+ closes out its 2023 cuts with a 188,000 bpd hike as oil sheds 7% on Iran talks

key_facts.fact: Seven OPEC+ countries — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman — met virtually on Aug 2 and agreed a production adjustment of 188,000 barrels per day to be implemented in September 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The seven participating countries decided to implement a production adjustment of 188 thousand barrels per day from the additional voluntary adjustments announced in April 2023. This adjustment will be implemented in September 2026.

key_facts.fact: The September increase completes the phased rollback of the 1.65 million bpd layer of voluntary cuts agreed in 2023; roughly 2 million bpd of 2022-vintage cuts remain in place until the end of the year.
key_facts.excerpt: The September increase agreed by core OPEC+ members ... finishes the phased rollback of a 1.65 million bpd supply cut originally agreed in 2023 ... OPEC+ still has one more layer of output cuts in place ... roughly 2 million bpd in cuts date back to 2022.

key_facts.fact: OPEC+'s Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee, meeting the same day, said attacks on energy assets during the US-Israeli war on Iran are expensive and time-consuming to repair and are hitting supply; the next meeting is set for Sept 6.
key_facts.excerpt: A separate OPEC+ meeting of a panel called the Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee also met ... and reiterated concern about attacks on energy assets during the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, saying they were expensive and time-consuming to repair.

key_facts.fact: Brent fell to $82.90 a barrel on Aug 3, down 5.72% on the day, after Trump called off the strike and said talks with Tehran would begin; US crude fell 6.93% to $78.80.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent fell to 82.91 USD/Bbl on August 3, 2026, down 5.71% from the previous day. ... | Crude Oil | 78.80 | -5.872 | -6.93% ... | Brent | 82.90 | -5.031 | -5.72% |

key_facts.fact: Brent for October delivery dropped as much as 7.3% in early Asian trading on Aug 3, briefly trading below $84, and European natural gas fell as much as 6.3%.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude for October delivery fell as much as 7.3%, dropping below $84 per barrel during early Asian trading ... European natural gas prices also declined sharply, falling as much as 6.3% in early trading.

key_facts.fact: Brent had risen about 24% in July, its biggest monthly gain since March, after hostilities resumed; analysts warn prices could reach $120 in the fourth quarter if free flow through Hormuz is not restored.
key_facts.excerpt: The recent flare-up sent oil prices soaring and Brent ended July with a more than 24 per cent gain, its biggest monthly advance since March this year. ... Analysts have warned crude prices could hit $120 per barrel in the fourth quarter if the free flow of energy supplies through the strait is not restored.

key_facts.fact: Many OPEC+ members cannot actually pump to their new targets: Russia is producing around 9 million bpd against a 9.8 million target, and Gulf exports remain hemmed in by the near-paralysis of the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: And in Russia, whose oil infrastructure has been repeatedly targeted by Ukrainian drone attacks, production is hovering at around nine million barrels per day -- compared with a target of 9.8 million barrels per day.

stories.headline: At least 72 dead after 60,000 crossed into Spain's Ceuta; EU calls emergency border meeting

key_facts.fact: An estimated 50,000 to 60,000 migrants, mostly young men, entered Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco between Wednesday and Friday — more than half the size of the city's 84,000 population.
key_facts.excerpt: Ceuta's population is just 84,000, but from Wednesday to Friday, an estimated 60,000 migrants entered the territory, Ceuta's top official Juan Jesus Vivas said. Spain's Ministry of Interior put the figure at 50,000.

key_facts.fact: Spanish authorities said on Sunday, Aug 2, that at least 72 migrants died, including drownings and deaths in a stampede at a breakwater; Morocco reported 11 deaths on its side and opened an investigation, blaming misinformation and traffickers.
key_facts.excerpt: At least 72 migrants died, including some who drowned and others who were killed in a stampede to cross a breakwater barrier, Spanish authorities said Sunday. Morocco reported 11 deaths on its side of the border ... The kingdom's authorities blamed misinformation and human traffickers for the breach, adding that they were opening an investigation.

key_facts.fact: Ireland, holding the rotating EU presidency, called an emergency video conference of the bloc's interior ministers for Tuesday after 22 of the EU's 27 member states signed a joint letter demanding coordinated action and stronger external borders.
key_facts.excerpt: Ireland, which holds the rotating EU presidency, said it had called an emergency video conference meeting of the bloc's interior ministers to discuss the crisis on Tuesday. The meeting was called after 22 of the EU's 27 member states issued a joint letter calling for 'coordinated action and the strengthening of external borders'.

key_facts.fact: Italy suspended its Schengen open-border policy with Spain, France announced a five-fold increase in police at its Spanish border, and Portugal said it would tighten southern land and maritime controls.
key_facts.excerpt: Meanwhile, Italy suspended its Schengen open-border policy with Spain. Madrid condemned the move ... France also announced a five-fold increase in the number of police at its border with Spain. Portugal also said it would beef up controls at its southern land and maritime borders.

key_facts.fact: Most of the migrants had walked back to Morocco by Sunday, with Spanish authorities still recovering bodies from the water; the US State Department raised its travel advisory for Ceuta to Level 3 on Saturday.
key_facts.excerpt: Most of the 60,000 migrants who swam, scrambled and later charged into the tiny Spanish exclave in North Africa this week had walked back to Morocco by Sunday ... Spanish authorities continued searching for bodies in the waters.

key_facts.fact: Vox leader Santiago Abascal visited Ceuta on Sunday calling the influx 'an invasion', while Pope Leo XIV said he was following the situation with concern; EPP leader Manfred Weber called on Saturday for Frontex to get real enforcement powers.
key_facts.excerpt: Santiago Abascal, the leader of the far-right Vox party, visited Ceuta on Sunday, slamming the Spanish government for the surge in migrant arrivals, which he called 'an invasion.' ... Pope Leo XIV on Sunday said he was 'following with concern the alarming situation in Ceuta.'

key_facts.fact: The scale dwarfed the previous mass crossing of May 2021, when about 12,000 people entered Ceuta over two days.
key_facts.excerpt: The scale of the influx was far bigger than the last such event in May 2021. Vivas said at the time that about 12,000 people crossed the border from Morocco into Ceuta over two days.

stories.headline: Ukraine hits Engels bomber base and three refineries deep inside Russia over the weekend

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck the Engels-2 air base near Saratov overnight into Aug 2, one of the main bases housing Russian strategic bombers, causing a fire; geolocated footage published Aug 2 shows the blaze.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian officials stated that Ukrainian forces struck the Engels-2 Air Base near Saratov City overnight. The Ukrainian General Staff reported that the strike caused a fire and noted that Engels-2 is one of the main Russian aviation bases housing strategic bombers.

key_facts.fact: The same wave hit the Saratov oil refinery, which has an annual refining capacity of about seven million tons, the Bashneft refinery in Ufa some 1,200 km from the border, and a tank farm at the Lyudinovskaya oil depot in Kaluga Oblast.
key_facts.excerpt: The Ukrainian General Staff noted that the Saratov Oil Refinery has an annual refining capacity of about seven million tons. ... Ukrainian forces also struck the Bashneft Oil Refinery in Ufa, Republic of Bashkortostan (about 1,200 kilometers from the international border), on August 2. ... Ukrainian forces also struck the tank farm of the Lyudinovskya oil depot in Kaluga Oblast overnight.

key_facts.fact: Drones also burned a Wildberries logistics warehouse in Samara Oblast, confirmed by the regional governor and the retailer's press office; Ukrainian drones separately struck the warehouses of online retailer Rozetka in Kyiv Oblast, hit by Russia twice in a day.
key_facts.excerpt: Samara Oblast Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev and Wildberries' press office confirmed the warehouse strike. ... Ukrainian online retailer Rozetka reported on August 2 that Russian Shahed-type drones struck its largest warehouse in Kyiv Oblast overnight – the second strike on the company's warehouses in the past day.

key_facts.fact: Russia launched 133 Shahed-, Gerbera- and Italmas-type drones plus Banderol loitering munitions and decoys overnight into Aug 2; Ukraine downed 109, while 24 strike drones hit 19 locations.
key_facts.excerpt: The Ukrainian Air Force reported that Russian forces launched 133 Shahed-type, Gerbera-type, and Italmas-type strike drones; Banderol loitering munitions; and Parodiya-type decoy drones ... Ukrainian forces downed 109 drones; that 24 strike drones hit 19 locations.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said on Aug 2 that in the previous week Russia struck 16 Ukrainian regions with about 1,900 drones, almost 1,600 glide bombs and 144 missiles; Russia's MoD claimed strikes on fuel tanks at Odesa port and on ships and infrastructure at Mykolaiv.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated on August 2 that Russian forces struck 16 Ukrainian regions and launched about 1,900 drones, almost 1,600 glide bombs, and 144 missiles in the past week (July 26 to August 1).

key_facts.fact: An improvised explosive device detonated in central Moscow City on Aug 1, potentially targeting Russian Aerospace Forces commander Colonel General Alexander Chayko; it was unclear whether he was killed or injured.
key_facts.excerpt: An improvised explosive device (IED) detonated in central Moscow City on August 1, potentially targeting Russian Aerospace Forces (VKS) Commander Colonel General Alexander Chayko. It is unclear as of this writing if the explosion killed or injured Chayko.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's public broadcaster reported on Monday, Aug 3, citing Zelensky, that Rustem Umerov — Kyiv's top negotiator in US-backed talks with Russia — will be appointed chief of the foreign intelligence service.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's Rustem Umerov, its top negotiator in US-backed talks with Russia, will be appointed chief of foreign intelligence, Ukraine's public broadcaster reported on Monday, citing President Volodymyr Zelensky.

stories.headline: Sharif's PML-N sweeps second phase of Pakistani Kashmir vote held under boycott and blackout

key_facts.fact: The second phase of Pakistan-administered Kashmir's three-phase regional election was held on Sunday, Aug 2, covering the Muzaffarabad division and the 12 disputed seats reserved for displaced Kashmiris, under heavy paramilitary deployment.
key_facts.excerpt: The Mirpur division voted on July 27, followed by the Muzaffarabad division and the 12 refugee constituencies on Sunday. ... The second phase of voting began at 8am (03:00 GMT) on Sunday under heavy security.

key_facts.fact: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's PML-N won 14 of the 18 seats contested in the second phase, taking it to 23 of 45 seats and a majority to form the regional government before the final phase on Aug 10.
key_facts.excerpt: The Pakistan Muslim League (Nawaz) swept the second phase of elections ... winning 14 out of 18 contested seats ... With the two phases taken together, PML-N has won 23 seats — the majority mark out of the 45 contested seats.

key_facts.fact: Residents and rights groups say the death toll from two months of protests has passed 50, including at least seven police and paramilitary personnel, while the banned Joint Awami Action Committee claims more than 60 civilians killed since June.
key_facts.excerpt: Residents and rights groups said the death toll has surpassed 50, including at least seven law enforcement personnel. The government has not shared an official death toll. The JAAC said more than 60 civilians have been killed since June.

key_facts.fact: The vote took place under an intermittent internet shutdown that has stretched beyond 50 days, disrupting campaigning and reporting; officials claimed turnout of nearly 50%, up from 46% in the first phase but below the 60%-plus of 2021 and 2016.
key_facts.excerpt: An intermittent internet shutdown stretching beyond 50 days has disrupted campaigning ... election officials claimed a turnout of nearly 50 percent, more than the 46 percent figure recorded in the first phase, but still less than the more than 60 percent recorded in the 2021 and 2016 elections.

key_facts.fact: The PPP alleged widespread rigging and said its worker Syed Mushtaq Shah was shot dead in a targeted attack on Sunday, a charge PML-N rejected; voting in three constituencies was postponed to Tuesday after landslides and blocked roads.
key_facts.excerpt: PPP, on the other hand, has alleged widespread rigging in Sunday's polls. ... Mughal said polling in three more seats, which were supposed to happen on Sunday, will now take place on Tuesday. 'Polling staff and election material could not reach the constituency because of landslides and bad weather that resulted in blocked roads.'

key_facts.fact: The unrest began after authorities banned the JAAC on June 5 over protests against prices and governance; the group's core demand is abolishing the 12 assembly seats reserved for refugees living elsewhere in Pakistan.
key_facts.excerpt: June 5: Authorities designate JAAC a 'proscribed organisation' under the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Anti-Terrorism Act, 2014. ... the protests are being held against the reservation of 12 seats in Pakistan-administered Kashmir's legislature for refugees from Indian-administered Kashmir who now live in other parts of Pakistan.

stories.headline: Dr. Reddy's wins US approval for its rituximab biosimilar, with Fresenius Kabi to sell it

key_facts.fact: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories announced on Aug 1 that the US FDA approved its rituximab biosimilar, a biosimilar to Roche's Rituxan, for the US market.
key_facts.excerpt: Hyderabad, India, August 1, 2026 – Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Ltd. (BSE: 500124, NSE: DRREDDY, NYSE: RDY, NSEIFSC: DRREDDY) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved its rituximab biosimilar, a biosimilar to Rituxan® (rituximab), for the U.S. market.

key_facts.fact: The approval followed a successful FDA Pre-License Inspection at the company's biologics manufacturing facility in Bachupally, Hyderabad.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval follows the successful recent Pre-License Inspection (PLI) conducted by the U.S. FDA at the Company's biologics manufacturing facility in Bachupally, Hyderabad.

key_facts.fact: Under an exclusive commercialization agreement, Fresenius Kabi holds the rights to market the product in the United States.
key_facts.excerpt: Under a commercialization agreement, Fresenius Kabi holds the exclusive rights to commercialize the product in the United States, one of the world's most important pharmaceutical markets.

key_facts.fact: The biosimilar is already sold in India, the European Union, the United Kingdom and more than 25 emerging markets, and has marketing approval in Switzerland and Canada; it is the company's sixth commercial biosimilar.
key_facts.excerpt: The rituximab biosimilar has been commercialized in India, the European Union, the United Kingdom and more than 25 emerging markets, and has also received marketing approval in Switzerland and Canada. ... Commercial biosimilars portfolio: six products

key_facts.fact: The FDA cleared the product on analytical, non-clinical and clinical evidence showing no clinically meaningful differences in safety, purity and potency versus Rituxan.
key_facts.excerpt: FDA approval was supported by analytical, non-clinical and clinical evidence showing the biosimilar is highly similar to the reference product. The data demonstrated no clinically meaningful differences in safety, purity and potency compared with Rituxan.

sources.title: Dr. Reddy's wins FDA nod for rituximab biosimilar
